utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you and good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Good morning to everyone as well. I would like to inform the parties that Judge Fluegge is for urgent personal reasons unable to continue sitting in this case and since we do not expect that it will be for a duration of more than five days, we have considered whether we are satisfied that it's in the interest of justice to continue to hear the case and Judge Moloto and myself have concluded that it is in the interest of justice. Therefore, we will sit 15 bis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Sokolovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we continue, I'd like to remind you that you are still bound by the solemn declaration that you gave yesterday at the beginning of your testimony. Mr. Traldi will now continue his cross-examination. Mr. Traldi, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Good morning, sir. And, sir, I want to begin by following up on two brief matters I brought up yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: First, can Exhibit P3913 be brought to the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And while it comes up, you testified yesterday at transcript page 26018 that: "This municipal assembly, as far as I know, did not hold a single session as such involving that composition." Now, when you gave that testimony, you were referring to the assembly created in December 1991 or as I'm going to call it the Serb assembly; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It held only one session in that year, 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And that was the session on the 26th of December; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose so. It was the end of that year.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You also met in 1992; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Including in April 1992?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So when you said yesterday, "This municipal assembly, as far as I know, did not hold a single session involving that composition," what did you mean?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean it was not in that year. In 1991 there was only one session as far as I know. That's about 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And actually that will obviate the need for this document, Your Honours. If I could have P3909.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And while that comes up, it's true that Serb members of the elected municipal assembly were, by establishment, also members of the Serb assembly; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps I should clarify this once again. The regular municipal assembly of Rogatica was set up after the multi-party elections in 1990, whereas the assembly of the Serbian people of the Serbian assembly, Serbian municipality of Rogatica was established towards the end of 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And just to make sure, you've confirmed, right, that Serb members of the elected assembly elected in 1990 were also, by establishment, members of the Serb assembly established in December 1991; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so, with a few more people included.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If we could have page 5 in the English and 4 in the B/C/S again. And I'm looking at the bottom of the page in the English and the second paragraph under Roman numeral 2 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, here it lists people who will be part of the assembly, and directing your attention to specific sentence, the document says: "Serb municipal assembly included also as per instructions of the main Serb democratic party board SDS village board presidents for from the area of the municipality." So those were the few more people that you just mentioned were included, right, SDS village board presidents?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And it's correct what it says here, that this assembly was set up pursuant to the instructions of the SDS main board; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose so, considering that I was not a member of the SDS, but from this paper we see that there were some instructions.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you were aware of those instructions at the time that you drafted this paper; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not really instructions. I only learned about it. The secretary of the assembly is the one who kept documents like this. I never saw them and I didn't need them.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can you just remind us who the secretary was?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mile Carkic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now next I want to turn to your testimony yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And if we could have, please, 65 ter 02559F.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I want to your turn to your testimony yesterday that most of the Muslims in Rogatica left in a convoy in April 1992. So this will be an excerpt from the census.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I would ask for page 2 in the B/C/S only. As Your Honours see, we haven't translated all of the numbers in English, of course. If we could look at line 17, that's Rogatica. And we're going to turn to the next page now also for line 17, page 3 in the B/C/S. On the left side under 1991, third column, we see there were more than 13.000 Muslims in Rogatica in 1991; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I hope this data is correct, but I have to correct you. You said that at that time the majority of Muslims left. I don't think I said it that way. I said that a half of the Muslims were already outside of Rogatica, about 3.000 in the area of Zepa and up to 3.000 left on buses and passenger cars towards Sarajevo. The situation was still more or less regular so that the number of Muslims in Rogatica was halved.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, sir, you testified yesterday that: "In this convoy," and I'm referring to transcript page 26011, "there were about 2.500 to 3.000 Muslims which indicates that most of the Muslim population completely freely decided to move towards Sarajevo." Do I understand your testimony just now to mean that you agree that 2.500 to 3.000 wasn't most of the Muslims in Rogatica municipality?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they were not the majority. And I must correct this. These were not exactly convoys, they were organised trips on buses and passenger cars, and I believe 2.500 to 3.000 residents left in this way completely of their own free will, abandoned Rogatica.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: When you say of their own free will, did you speak to any of them about why they were leaving?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd tender this excerpt.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit P6772, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, I'm going to turn to a new topic now. And could we please have 65 ter 31353 for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: This is a record of an interview with Mile Ujic conducted by the Rogatica police on the 6th of June 2004. Mr. Ujic was a member of your Crisis Staff and of the Executive Committee in Rogatica; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was president of the Executive Board in Rogatica from that regular assembly in 1990 until I was elected in the middle of 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: He was also the minister of industry in SAO Romanija; right? The SAO being the Serb autonomous region of Romanija.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly. I don't know the details, however, because I was not an activist in that period, in that kind of organising.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If we turn to the top of page 3 in the English and the middle of page 2 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Mr. Ujic is describing a Serbian assembly session at Sjemec, and he says beginning about six lines down in the English: "I went there, but I was surprised by an agenda of the meeting, since the first item on the agenda was appointment of the president of Executive Committee. This appeared a bit absurd to me since I was the president of the Executive Committee but at the same time it surprised all other members and most of the members who did not understand what was this all about. After a brief indignation at the proposed agenda members accepted it, and I only told them that they should first remove me from the office and then appoint a new president since I was legitimately elected president of the Executive Committee. However, what happened happened. The agenda was accepted, the new president, Milorad Sokolovic was elected with explanation that I was too soft and too accommodating in negotiations and that someone more rough should be appointed." Now, is Mr. Ujic telling the truth here about why you were selected to replace him?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the way he sees that session. I have to say I was invited to that session, first of all, as a deputy. The assembly session had been convened by the president and his associates. I came to the session and somebody nominated me. I don't know -- I don't know the details. I was elected at a legitimate session. I would not agree that I belonged to any hard line, and I know Mr. Ujic very well and I don't think that he was a hard liner in any way himself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can I just get a clarification. Mr. Sokolovic, at page 6, line 21, you say: "The assembly session had been convened by the president and his associates." When you say "president," who do you mean? Do you mean the same Mr. Ujic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, he was not the president of the municipal assembly, that was Mr. Tomislav Antonic, he was president of the assembly. Mile Ujic was president or chairman of the Executive Board.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: When you say president of the assembly, you're referring to the Serb assembly rather than the elected assembly; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I mean the Serbian assembly. Because Mr. Batinic was vice-president of this regular municipal assembly from 1990.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And just for the purposes of the transcript, sir, at line 9 today, you were recorded to say Tomislav Antonic was president of the Serb assembly, did you mean to say Tomislav Batinic with a B?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Batinic. Batinic is the name, Tomislav the first name.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, I want to turn now to the negotiations --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we do so, you say that the reasons stated, that's the view of the person who was interviewed, and you said I was elected legitimately. But what was the reason to get rid of the old president and to elect you as the new president?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would not like to explain that in detail. It was a legitimate body, the municipal assembly. It had its legal bodies. I was nominated and I accepted that position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You don't have to explain in detail but some explanation, I would appreciate.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Really, believe me, I don't know what I could say except that I was already a prominent political figure by that time. I had been already president of the assembly for two terms of office, and that must be the reason why people held me in high esteem, I would say, and why they nominated me to such high office.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But it still doesn't explain why there was a change at all.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Really, it was not up to me, the municipal assembly was a lawful body with its auxiliary bodies and they decided that I was good for that position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Again, you've told us now several times that it was a lawful body and that you were legitimately elected, but it still does not explain why the old president had to leave and why there was any need to have a new president.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You should really ask the president of the assembly and the president of the Serbian Democratic Party which was in a way the main political component at that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You were just sitting there and it all happened to you and you never gave it a thought or you never heard why there was a need to replace the former president?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I had been asked before the session while the agenda was being prepared whether I was willing to take up that position because people who dealt with personnel policy were already thinking about putting me in that place, and I did not display any interest in why my predecessor Mile Ujic was being replaced.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, you say this was the way he saw it, but if you do not know why he was replaced, you couldn't say that he is wrong, isn't it? Because you didn't know any reason apart from that they elected you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's the way he sees it. And I was not in a position to discuss my predecessor Mile Ujic and that's why I didn't think it's right for me to explain why I was nominated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So he explains in the statement why he was replaced. You have no clue as to what triggered the replacement of the former president. So whether he's right or wrong, you can't tell us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Precisely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, just to follow up on one of the answers you gave. You testified today at transcript page -- temporary transcript page 9 that you had been asked before the session while the agenda was being prepared whether you were willing to take up the position of president of the Executive Committee. Who asked you?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mainly talked to the president of the municipal assembly in the preparation for this session, Mr. Tomislav Batinic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you mentioned when you were asked about the reasons that you were chosen to replace Mr. Ujic, you said: "You should really ask the president of the assembly," that's Mr. Batinic, "and the president of the Serbian democratic party." Who was the president of the Serbian Democratic Party in Rogatica at that time?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, I believe it was Mr. Sveto Veselinovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Unless the Judges have any other questions on this matter, I would move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just one short question. You said you talked to the president of the municipal assembly. Was he the one who asked you to make yourself available as president?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I talked to him and I believe he had previously spoken to their leadership of the SDS because they were the only important political factor at the time, and they probably made some assessment from the point of view of personnel policy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Repeatedly you said you talked to him, but he was the one who asked you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, he did, because the session was being prepared and I gave my approval, my consent, that if I'm nominated, I'll accept.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, when you refer to the leadership of the SDS, leadership at the local level, leadership at the republican level, what did you refer to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My only contact was with the leaders of the SDS at the local level.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That was not my question. You said: "I believe he had previously spoken to their leadership of the SDS because they were the only important political factor." Leadership at what level, that was the only important political factor, local level or higher up?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think concerning these matters only at the local level. It's possible they had other consultations that I didn't know about, but it was mainly the local representatives of the Serbian Democratic Party.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you know it or do you believe it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I was not in a position to have contact with higher levels of the SDS.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you don't know it, it's just assuming that it may have been at a higher level, it could have been at the local level as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right, because generally speaking I believe it was at the local level. Whether they had any other consultations, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, I want to turn to the negotiations that Mr. Ujic mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And I'll be asking for 65 ter 31322.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: While it comes up, in paragraph 9 of your statement, you talk about the agreement on the division of Rogatica municipality, and in paragraph 10 you say, after the agreement: "This situation lasted until the St. George's day or approximately for two months. The first killings of Serbs by artillery missiles occurred in 1992 in the area of Borike. The next significant event happened on 21 May 1992." Now, in connection with that evidence, I'd like to look at this report which is from the Serbian municipality of Rogatica Executive Board and says it's to, among others, the Presidency of the Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could we briefly have page 3 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Do you recognise the signature?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This signature is mine, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If we could turn to page 2 in the English, second paragraph, and page 1 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And this paragraph reads: "The agreement on the partition of the territory of Rogatica municipality into a Serbian and Muslim municipality was rendered invalid by the Serbian Assembly of Rogatica municipality in its decision of 18 May 1992 because the war conflicts broke out." Now, you don't mention in your statement that the Serbian assembly of Rogatica abrogated the agreement, do you?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't mention that in that statement but everything that is written can be read and that can jog one's memory.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So this is correct, isn't it, that the Serbian assembly withdrew from the agreement on the 18th of May, 1992?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, that is what is written here so that's the way it's got to be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Sokolovic, you said: "I don't mention that in that statement, but everything that is written can be read and that can jog one's memory." Your statement should contain the whole truth irrespective of whether we read other documents. So don't give us half of the story and then say you can read elsewhere what the whole truth was. Is that clear to you? You can't just select part of what is the truth so as to say we agreed on partition, and then say you can read somewhere else that we abdicated this agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, did we follow the same principle during the testimonies of the Prosecution witnesses? Did we follow the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Whenever I find that a witness gives us half of the story where important elements are known to the witness and when the witness says I didn't tell it because you can read it elsewhere, if that would happen, I would have reacted. I don't know whether it happened from my recollection, but I certainly would have reminded the witness that he should tell the whole truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We can start from one of the first witnesses of the Prosecution, Mr. Harland. If you want to check what --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I will check. Give me the --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- he said in his statement and what we found in the documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I will certainly look at it if you give me the details of --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You can [Overlapping speakers]. Mr. Harland, anything I asked him for seven hours was not in his statement and everything was even different from what was written in his statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did he ever say you can read it elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So we should find that phrase to be able to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, no, no, no, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- to question at the Prosecution witnesses?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I take --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I don't think this is fair approach to our --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, Witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness. Mr. Lukic --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I'm not used to being interrupted. I give you a full opportunity to tell us what you want to tell us. If you say please read Mr. Harland's testimony and compare the situation with the one we are facing at this moment, I'll certainly do that. So therefore -- and if there was a difference in approach, if it was -- well, to say not unfair to this witness, but if we have been too lenient for Mr. Harland, then I certainly will look at that and I'll consider it and put it on the record if need be.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Or you can see Mr. Higgs, their expert.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Give me --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I can give you every single one, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The cross-examination wouldn't be necessary if everything is there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's why we have cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then you misunderstand, unfortunately, Mr. Lukic, what the difference is between the present situation and the ordinary situation of cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, I understand perfectly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Cross-examination is there to test the evidence of the witness. But as soon as a witness says, "I only gave you half of the story because I felt that you could read the whole of the story elsewhere," that is different from normal cross-examination. I do agree with you that in cross-examination, the evidence of the witness will be tested, but here I responded to a specific observation by this witness, give me the sources, the exact references on where we, in your view, behaved not as we should have done, and we'll read it and we'll look at it. But until now, to say what happens here, cross-examination is not needed any how, if you would adopt my views on what a witness is expected to tell as the whole truth, I disagree with you on that respect. But again, I will re-read every single instance, every single instance you will refer to. You may proceed, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: One more observation, Your Honour, I'm sorry. Whatever witness said was truth. It was very short statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I didn't say it was not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: He --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, you are revisiting. If you want to further -- if you want to further deal with the matter while giving the references, you can also make submissions as to the matters you are raising now. Mr. Traldi may now proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I want to turn to the end of this same paragraph. The last sentence reads: "Because the war conflict broke out the Serbian Assembly of Rogatica municipality took the decision to declare the entire territory of the former Rogatica municipality a Serbian municipality." Now, you don't mention in your statement that after withdrawing from the agreement, the Serb assembly of Rogatica declared all of the territory of Rogatica to be Serb territory, do you?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well that is what this decision says. But I would just like to ask you something kindly, Mr. President. I am not a lawyer. I am a technical person, if you will. As for this statement that I signed, the people who helped me thought that it was sufficient for me to give answers to certain questions on the basis of an outline, so I am not a professional and I'm not really trained to write a long paper on this. It's been more than 20 years now and I remember quite a few things, but I have to say that I will always and invariably be telling the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, just to be perfectly clear, what I'm putting to you is that in your statement, you haven't given a complete and accurate picture of the events surrounding the agreement on dividing the territory. That you cannot properly understand that agreement without knowing that the Serb assembly withdrew from it and claimed the entire municipality as Serb territory. That's true, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to remind you of this. When we started discussing a solution to the problem, the two sides, the Muslim and the Serb sides, we said that we should do everything possible to avoid a conflict. If killing starts then all talks end because killing is an act that prevents talks. So all of this is after the well-known killings of Serbs committed by Muslims. And then all talks stopped after this Serb patrol was attacked. After that, the representatives of the Muslims said you cannot get the body until there are 15 corpses, and I said thank you very much, we're not going to talk anymore. And after this happened, we did not talk anymore at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, actually, sir, the negotiations about the body you just mentioned, that's in your statement and that refers to Drazenko Mihajlovic; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You said he was killed on the 21st of May, that's after this decision to claim the entire municipality, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I really cannot link that up now unless you remind me of the dates, because I know full well when this happened, all of this in relation to the death of Drazen Mihajlovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, you say here in the third line of this paragraph that the decision to withdraw was taken on the 18th of May, the decision by the Serb assembly to withdraw from the agreement was taken on the 18th of May, 1992. That's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's probably right because that's what is written there. I cannot have any information that would be better.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you say in paragraph 10 of your statement, D652, in pertinent part, that: "The next significant event happened on 21 May 1992 when a Serb patrol came across an ambush in the territory controlled by the Serb majority in the municipality of Rogatica when Drazenko Mihajlovic was killed." So I have two questions about that sentence. First, that's on the 21st, that's after this decision to withdraw from the agreement; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in terms of the date, yes, but before that, there was St. George's day when the first killings started.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And second, in that sentence you refer to "territory controlled by the Serb majority." The Serbs were of course not a majority in the municipality of Rogatica, were they?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were not.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And just to complete our discussion of the two assemblies from yesterday, from this point, when the agreement was withdrawn from by the Serb assembly, it was the Serb assembly that made -- that met that made decisions about life in the municipality of Rogatica; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And it's the Serb assembly that you're describing here, as well in your report that we looked at earlier this morning; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I tender this document 65 ter 31322.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit P6773, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P6773 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, we've discussed some of the early conflict. There was a large-scale attack on Muslim areas of Rogatica by Bosnian Serb forces just a few days after the Serb assembly withdrew from the agreement; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that that was after the killing of Drazenko Mihajlovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Very shortly after, right around the 22nd and 23rd of May?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And I'd put to you that many Muslims left those areas in response to that attack. That's true, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't think so. Because, for instance, the biggest settlement, the town of Rogatica, my mother, my sister, and so on lived there then and these Muslims who were majority in town, and they all stayed even after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And the settlements that were attacked, the Muslim settlements that were attacked, do you know if the residents stayed or not?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you see, I assume that perhaps in that area where Mihajlovic was killed that part of the Muslims left then. However, I have to tell you what happened afterwards. After this happened, the Muslim leadership decided to move out of Rogatica slowly, led, for example, by the president of the municipal assembly of Rogatica. Immediately after that, they were relocated. They went a few kilometres out of Rogatica. And after that, they did not return to Rogatica. They continued towards Medjedja going through Muslim villages. That is one wing and the other wing one went westward, again led by some military officers and so on, and then they would pass through the municipality of Rogatica across the Praca river then Ustipraca and then further up, and I understand that that was an instruction. They were the majority there and they left.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm going to ask that the court officer call up Exhibit P352 now. This is one of General Mladic's notebooks.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And while it comes up, sir, we were discussing abrogating the agreement, withdrawing from the agreement about division of the municipality. Was that decided spontaneously on the 18th or had you and other members of the Serb assembly been discussing it beforehand?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you see, always when preparing a certain gathering, these preparations have to be carried out. If there is a municipal assembly session it has to be prepared. The agenda has to be set and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: About how long before the 18th had the discussions about withdrawing from the agreement been going on, one day, several days, several weeks?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think you could have been only, I don't know, seven days. I don't think it's ten days just because things got so complicated after the 6th of May, after this first attack against the Serbs in the municipality of Rogatica.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could we have page 349 in the English and page 357 in the B/C/S of this document. And this time I think I've given the page for the B/C/S transcript and we've gotten the B/C/S original. If we could have the other B/C/S version. And I'm sorry, I should have been more specific.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is the typewritten B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: The typewritten B/C/S version, yeah. I think I did it the other way last time and it's possible the Registry and I have both tried to adjust to each other and wound up with the opposite problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We see here in the middle of the page note 17 May 1992 Sokolac, 1200 hours, talks with representatives of Rogatica, Olovo, Han Pijesak, Pale, and the Belgrade people from this area. Now, before moving on, this is a meeting that we'll see was also attended by President Karadzic and by Mr. Krajisnik the president of the Bosnian Serb Assembly, did you also attend this meeting as one of the representatives from Rogatica?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not remember attending such a meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now turning to page 351 in the English and 359 in the B/C/S transcript, we see President Karadzic speaking and he says: "We're looking for results from the army, that's their job." Were you told that he had said this at the meeting?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know about anything like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could we have P3176, please. This will be an article about the same meeting. Or a meeting between the same senior officials and representatives of the same areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And if I could direct your attention to point 5 on page 2 in both languages. It refers to Mr. Krajisnik's remarks. And it says that he "stressed that the time is ripe for a demarcation of the areas between Croats, Serbs, and Muslims because as he said a common state with them is no longer possible not because we do not want that but because that is what they want." So my question for you is you have said that you began discussing your intentions to abrogate the agreement which resulted in claiming the entire Rogatica municipality several days before this meeting. Do you know if any of the Rogatica representatives who were at this meeting informed Karadzic, Krajisnik, Mladic, and the other RS leaders present of their intentions to claim the entire municipality of Rogatica?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I repeat once again, I don't think I attended the meeting and I don't know about this. I mean, I don't know that this discussion happened. Or at least I do not recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Do you know who would have been the Rogatica representatives to such a meeting?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I assume that these more significant meetings, if I can put it that way, were attended by people from the SDS, that they were invited. I imagine it could have been the president of the SDS, the president of the Serb assembly, and so on, Serb municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm about to turn to a new topic. I see we're just a minute or two short of the break and for continuity I'd request that we break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, let's take the break now. Could you tell us how much time you'd need after the break?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: It's been a little bit difficult to predict how long an answer will take. I anticipate I will be done in the next session but probably towards the end of the session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll take the break after the witness has left the courtroom. We'd like to see you back, Mr. Sokolovic, in 20 minutes from now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We resume at ten minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Just one brief follow-up on the meeting we discussed on May 17th immediately before the break. You testified at transcript -- temporary transcript page 22, line 12, that Messrs. Batinic and Veselinovic were among the people likely to attend such a meeting and you identified them by their titles, the president of the SDS and the president of the Serb municipality or the Serb assembly. And they discussed military issues at this meeting. Was Rajko Kusic also one of the people who would be likely to attend such a meeting?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of call, Rajko is Kusic with a K, if that's who you are speaking of. As for the meeting, I don't know about it. I don't know who was there. I certainly wasn't there, so I can't say anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, if we could have P3909 again. And I'll be looking at page 28 in the English and page 25 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm interested in the paragraph that reads: "The administrative authority, i.e., the refugee committee, commenced, in accordance with the existing regulations of Republika Srpska, to find temporary accommodation for refugees in deserted apartments and houses by issuing special decisions on such temporary accommodation." Now, many of those deserted apartments and houses had been deserted by their Muslim inhabitants who'd left Rogatica; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, an immense amount of deserted Muslim property in Rogatica was plundered, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now if we could turn to page 32 in the English and 29 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, point 9 is where you discuss the plunder of deserted Muslim property. I'm actually going to direct your attention to the second paragraph under the point. And you write here: "The greatest responsibility for the situation elaborated under points 8 and 9," point 9 again being the plunder of deserted Muslim property, "The greatest responsibility falls upon the command of Rogatica Brigade." What did you mean that the command of the Rogatica Brigade bore the greatest responsibility for the plunder of the deserted Muslim property?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand what -- what is the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can you explain to us why you said that the greatest responsibility for the immense plunder of deserted Muslim property fell upon the command of the Rogatica Brigade? What made you write that?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because there was a tight co-operation with the command -- between the command of the Rogatica Brigade and the police. The police were less numerous. The brigade was numerically the strongest and some of them behaved in a very lax way and that was the distinction between them and the policemen who were relatively few.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If we could look back at point 6, and it will be at the top of the page in B/C/S and in English, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We read that: "Cooperation with the command of the brigade of Rogatica was not achieved fully and sufficiently, especially recently, and that thanks to the incorrect behaviour of its commander, and especially after he gained rank and medals, with which the incorrect behaviour got worse." Now that commander was Mr. Rajko Kusic; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And what was the incorrect behaviour you were referring to here?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we were thinking of his day-to-day attitude and behaviour. The civilian authority's importance was often minimised, and when you give people weapons it tends to change their behaviour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I want to turn now to what happened to those Muslim civilians who you say stayed in Rogatica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before you do so, just for the record, Mr. Sokolovic, can you tell us of which army was this Rogatica Brigade a unit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Rogatica Brigade was part of the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, sir, Muslim civilians were in fact detained at several locations in Rogatica; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would not say that they were detained, especially not all of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: The municipal assembly received communications from this Rogatica Brigade confirming that Muslim civilians were being held in several locations in Rogatica, didn't you? And of course I mean the Serb assembly here.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, we already know that the municipal assembly convenes by itself and there are officials who do their work such as the secretary of the assembly, the president of the assembly, et cetera. As for that awareness, as far as I remember, the secondary school centre was one such place organised by the police or the army, I don't know. I know that it wasn't organized by the assembly. It was one place where people could find shelter, both the Serbs and the Muslims and the few Croats that lived there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Let's look at one of the communications that the Rogatica Brigade sent to the assembly.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could we have 65 ter 085851 [Realtime transcript read in error "05851"].

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So this is a report --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: 8581, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Just to correct it on the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: This is a report from the Rogatica Brigade to the municipal assembly of Rogatica dated the 30th of November, 1992. Directing your attention to the bottom left-hand corner in the B/C/S version, do you recognise the signature confirming receipt?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know. I think it's about Nada Sinsija. She was one of the desk officers at the administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, one of the people who would have reviewed a report like this is the president of the Executive Committee; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, because everybody had their own post office box. Mail for the municipal assembly was addressed to the president, and the other addressee had his own post office box. The commander had his own mail coming to his own address. I don't remember that I've ever seen this letter before.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Let's look at the document briefly and see if it refreshes your recollection. Reading from the top, Captain Kusic says: "Since the first day of combat activities, the members of Rogatica Brigade have treated civilian population according to the Geneva Convention. We have separated civilian population from extreme combatants we have fought against. With your approval, we have gathered civilians at the secondary school, church centre, and socially owned enterprise, Ergela, in Rogatica." Do you see that text?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see that, but this text relates to the president of the municipal assembly, I suppose, not me.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Were you aware that civilians were being detained in those locations?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew that people gathered in the secondary school centre not only Muslims in the conviction they would find shelter there from all sorts of tensions and friction. And as for the rest, I did not have any involvement or contact in that. This is a question more for the police that was in charge of law enforcement and the commander of the Rogatica Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: When you say the secondary school centre, we're discussing the Veljko Vlahovic school; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, did you ever go there yourself?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, the Chamber's received evidence in, for example, Exhibit P309, that in fact the civilians in the Vlahovic school were not treated according to the Geneva Conventions but were subjected to beatings, rape, and torture, and some were taken out of the school and killed. That's true, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't confirm anything considering that I did not participate, I did not visit, nor did the Executive Board ever discuss these matters. You should ask the police and the army, or rather the command, and here, of course, people who have their bad experiences or otherwise.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, in the next paragraph, the document says: "After a sufficient number of civilian population was gathered you," which I take to mean the municipal assembly, "have organised their transport to Sarajevo, Bijeljina, Olovo, and to Zepa which was escorted by civilian police." So it's correct, isn't it, that the civilian authorities together with the civilian police, organised transport of these people out of detention facilities and out of Rogatica municipality.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You should ask the president of the municipal assembly and his associates. The Executive Board of Rogatica municipality never dealt with this matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm not asking at the moment whether you dealt with this matter. I'm asking, you were aware, weren't you, that convoys of people were being organized by the assembly out of Rogatica from these locations.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't know any details. And again, you have to make a distinction between the Executive Board and the president of the municipality and his associates. I repeat again, the Executive Board did not deal with this matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I think you're reiterating in response to a number of these questions that you don't believe this was under your personal area of responsibility. When I ask whether you know if something happened or not, I'm not asking whether it was in your area of responsibility, simply whether you know that it happened. And if I'm interested in whether it was part of your job, I'll ask about that specifically. Can we agree to proceed that way?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you see, as a citizen --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection. I believe this is asked and answered in response to the previous question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm fairly sure that's the first time I've asked the witness if he could agree to proceed in that fashion, so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Your objection is denied.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Directing your attention to the last paragraph of the document. It reads: "We would like to mention that you have the lists of the loyal Muslims in the area of Rogatica municipality as well as the lists of the ones who were sent away from Rogatica in the previous months during combat activities. Therefore, you possess the information required by Republika Srpska Presidency." Now, were you aware that the Serb assembly in Rogatica was in possession of lists of loyal Muslims and of Muslims who had been sent away?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not know as president of the Executive Board, but the president of the municipal assembly should have to respond to the question whether he had any communication on the subject and whether he received these papers.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be P6774, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P6774 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And I'd ask for 65 ter 08281.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And this is a report from the RS MUP in 2004. And we see in the first paragraph that it is the result of a process of gathering information regarding collection centres where persons of Bosniak nationality stayed in the region of Rogatica. And it says the following information was gathered. The first paragraph refers to a building of the former nursery garden and that was known as Rasadnik; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose so. There's a lot of text here. I would have to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you need more time to read it, you'll have an opportunity to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now the second paragraph, sir, refers to the malt house building which it says was also the seat of the body known as the Crisis Staff. Now, you testified yesterday at transcript page 26015 that after St. George's day 1992 you were present at the malt house building every day unless you had a business trip or a meeting somewhere else. Do you recall that testimony?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let's clear one thing up. The building of the Sladara factory --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, the question was whether you recall that you gave that testimony yesterday. Could you please confirm that you do recall or say I don't remember that I gave testimony as presented by counsel.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I repeat, the seat of the Crisis Staff and the municipal organs of Rogatica as of St. George's day was in the malt factory as opposed to the Ergela, the stables building, which is in a different location.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but that wasn't the question. There's no dispute about that. Do you recall that yesterday you testified that after St. George's day in 1992, you were present at the malt house building every day unless you had a business trip or a meeting somewhere else. That's the question, whether you remember that you told us that yesterday, your presence at the malt house factory or the malt house building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I remember that and I confirm it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, you were aware that people were detained in the same building where the Crisis Staff was headquartered, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No people were detained in that factory.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, I want to point you to the example of one specific detainee, Mehmed Agic, and the Krajisnik trial judgement made the following finding at paragraph 680: "On 21 June 1992, 'Chetniks' in olive drab uniform captured Witness Agic who had been involved in organising the defence in Rogatica before the shelling." That's Mehmed Agic; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am aware that Mehmed Agic was arrested somewhere there, but he was not kept or even interrogated in the offices of that factory in the same part of that building that was occupied by the municipal organs of Rogatica, and he was certainly not detained. Just one more thing. It's a large building. It's possible that in some part of the building he was kept, but in the area of the building occupied by the administration of Rogatica, there was nobody detained.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Who occupied the other areas of the building?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was all part of an industrial complex. I don't know even how much space it occupied. But the Executive Board and the rest of the administration of Rogatica occupied the office space that previously belonged to the general manager. That's where I and my associates worked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, you were not asked about where you were. You were asked about who occupied the other parts of the building. If you know, tell us; if you don't know, tell us as well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, you said the Executive Board. On the 21st of June, 1992, in fact it would have been the Crisis Staff that was still in operation; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was done in parallel because the Crisis Staff met only from time to time. Most of them had their work assignments, whereas I acted also as president of the Crisis Staff and president of the Executive Board and later I was elected president of the Executive Board.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So is it your evidence now that you do not know whether civilians were detained in the building that also served as the headquarters of the Crisis Staff and the Executive Board?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that building, such persons were certainly never detained.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And Mr. Agic, your evidence is you don't -- you said about a page ago that there were other areas of the building. Is it your evidence that you don't know whether he was detained there? Or is it your evidence that he -- that you know he was not detained there?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll try to be more precise. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now can 65 ter 31352 [Realtime transcript read in error "31312"] be brought to the screens.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, you started reading from a trial judgement which did not in any way touch upon the building. I don't know whether you pursue that or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sorry, and you're right. To be fully fair to the witness, I think I ought to say that judgement, that paragraph of the judgement continues that they beat Mr. Agic and took him to the Sladara malt house in Rogatica where they detained him for two or three days. Now, the witness had confirmed or -- that he knew he was arrested and stated that he didn't know whether he was detained there which was why I didn't finish the paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: But, sir, if you have any additional comment on that finding.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have any comments except for this knowledge that I have. I knew Mr. Agic personally. I know that he was arrested. I know that he was exchanged, I think, and I think I saw him once or twice after the war. We did not talk about that at all, though.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What did you say the 65 ter number is that you are calling for?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: The next one will be 31352.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And while --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It was wrongly recorded.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, or you misspoke. I don't --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: No, I've got it correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. But a mistake was made somewhere. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm willing to concede it's likely to have been mine. While it comes up, I'd tender the previous document, 65 ter 08281.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, Mr. Registrar tells me P3339 might be the same document.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We'll check that and I'll withdraw my request for the moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You can still call it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You can still call it if you want to put any questions to the witness about it, and then we'll find out whether it's the same document. So whether the witness answered then your questions on the basis of the 65 ter document or on exactly the same admitted exhibit can be changed letter.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sorry, I hadn't understood whether it's the same document as what I've called to the screen or as the exhibit that I just tendered?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, I think it was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The 65 ter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- the 65 ter number you just mentioned, that that was a document which was quite a while ago admitted as P3339.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I would not call it a comedy of errors but rather a tragedy of errors. It's 2229 and not as I said before, 3339.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And that does refer to the previous document, and so I would withdraw my request to re-tender it at this stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: By previous document you mean 08281?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: According to Ringtail on our screens, yes. According to the e-court system.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that was then another error on my side. Let's now look at the document you asked for.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: This is Mr. Agic's statement which he swore under oath was truthful. Now, if we could have page 5 in the English, and I believe also in the B/C/S. Sorry, I've provided the wrong B/C/S page number. I imagine I'll be -- I've been corrected already.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So we have the correct page now. And we see him describing his arrest. Now, directing your attention to roughly the middle of the page in the B/C/S, the name is hard to read, but do you see the name Radisav also known as Pjano at the beginning of the line on the left? And that's Radisav Ljubinac?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ljubinac, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And it describes that Ljubinac and other soldiers dressed in camouflage and olive drab started insulting Mr. Agic and others calling us Ustashas and beating us all over with a rubber truncheon. Now, that's at the time of his arrest. I want to look a few lines further down, and it says: "They pushed us into the APC and took us to the Sladara in Rogatica where they had their barracks at that time." Now there's only one Sladara malt house factory in Rogatica; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I again wish to recall the following. I have a feeling that things are not being understood properly. As far as I know, the command of the Rogatica Brigade was in the facilities of Ergela and other organisations, and this was a separate entity in relation to the malt factory Sladara. My impression from this letter is that all of this could have happened only on the premises of the Ergela. Even Upitrans used to be the owner of that facility. It's in the northern part of Rogatica. But it does not belong to the compound of the malt factory.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Witness, once again, the question was: "There is only one Sladara malt house factory in Rogatica; right?" The answer is either "yes" or a "no" or "I don't know."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There was just one malt factory but these events did not take place in the malt factory, Sladara.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This brings me to another matter, Mr. Traldi. The witness told us that he was aware that this person was arrested. On all the other questions, it seems that he has hardly any knowledge about what followed and he contradicts this statement on a basis which is unknown to this Chamber. Now, I don't know what you are heading for, but if the witness doesn't know anything about this arrest and what then followed, then you can put seven statements to him, doesn't make any sense. I'm not knowing where you are heading for but I just would like to bring this to your attention, that if you pursue this line of questioning then of course you must end up somewhere you may be aware of the Chamber is not at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I am intending to end up there in the next two questions or so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So I have only one more point in the document to show.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's fine. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now turning to the top of page 6 in the English, and the sixth line down, and also I believe the top of the next page in the B/C/S. That's page 12.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We read: "Soon afterwards, Kusic, Ujic, and two or three of their henchmen went to the room opposite us and started beating Milic and two members of the Hodzic family asking for information about the couriers for Zepa." Now, at this time Mr. Kusic and Mr. Ujic were members of your Crisis Staff as well as officers in the Rogatica Brigade; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were members of the Crisis Staff all the time, but especially Mr. Kusic did not attend sessions very often. I've already said that about half of those 20 members usually attended, about 11 or 12. Mr. President, I would like to recall something else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, please just answer the questions. The question was whether they were members of the Crisis Staff as well as officers in the Rogatica Brigade. There was no question about how often they attended meetings. You confirm that they were members and that they were also officers in the Rogatica Brigade. Then please put your next question to the witness, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So I'd put to you that what this statement reflects is that members of the Crisis Staff you were president of abused a prisoner in the building that served as the headquarters of the Crisis Staff at the time. You must have been aware of that, mustn't you?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not correct. There was never any mistreatment on the premises that were used by the municipal assembly at the malt factory. Again, I wish to recall that these were two separate facilities.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, when you say these were two separate facilities, are you suggesting that you believe these events may have occurred at Ergela where the Rogatica Brigade's barracks were?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, possibly. You see the command of the Rogatica Brigade, I'm going to be very specific now, was in the premises of Upitrans and Ergela was opposite that facility. And both facilities were used by the military. I really cannot speak about any details. They certainly know what they used for what. But they certainly did not do any of their work at the premises in Sladara, the malt factory, where the Crisis Staff was.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could we have 65 ter 31333.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And, sir, this is a record of an interview you gave to the Rogatica police in 2004. And looking at the bottom of the page in the English, we see you told them: "The Crisis Staff was an organ that did not deal with operational, military, and police tasks, nor was it informed about the activities of the police and army." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Turn to the top of the next -- or turn to the next paragraph. I think it may be the top of the next page in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You state that in view of that fact you have no information regarding the military police and paramilitary formations that were active in the area of the Rogatica municipality in that period. Now, we've seen that the municipal assembly received reports from the Rogatica Brigade at a time when you were a member. You've told us where the barracks are. You've told us that officers in the brigade served as part of your Crisis Staff. So I'd put to you that you were not truthful with the Rogatica police when you stated this and in fact you do have knowledge about the military police and paramilitary formations in Rogatica in 1992.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not have any such information in terms of official communication or any kind of reporting to the Crisis Staff, if I can put it that way. I state with full responsibility that the police did their work, the military did their work, and the Executive Board of the municipality of Rogatica carried out their work within the civilian domain.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Is it your position that the military never provided reports or updates to the Executive Committee on the work they were doing in their domain?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think they didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could 65 ter 31354 be brought to the screen, and this will be the last document that I show the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, this is a letter to the 1st Podrinje Light Infantry Brigade command from the Republika Srpska municipality of Rogatica Executive Committee dated 30 November 1992. Do you recognise the signature on the bottom right part of the B/C/S?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it's my signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, the first paragraph reads: "At the session attended by the president of the municipal assembly, held on 28th November 1992, the municipality of Rogatica Executive Committee was informed about the letter, strictly confidential number 69/92, dated 14th November, 1992, submitted to the Rogatica municipal assembly by the 1st Podrinje Light Infantry Brigade on the 17th of November, 1992." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And turning to page 2 in the English, last paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We read, and you write: "Therefore, the Executive Committee invites the brigade command on this occasion, too, to discuss every current problem with representatives of the municipal assembly, Executive Committee, or administration organs and try to find a joint solution for certain problems." Do you see that as well?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So I'd put to you that this reflects that you did, in fact, receive reports about what the brigade was doing in its military domain, and you did, in fact, in your official capacity communicate with the brigade about issues and try to find joint solutions to certain problems. That's true, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you see, I really need to see this letter to see what the answer is. We had active communication with the command and -- sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, if you say "I need to read the whole letter, otherwise I can't answer your questions." Then you will be given an opportunity to do so. I also could imagine on the basis of the text that was read to you that you could already answer the question, but if you consider it necessary to read the whole of the letter, a copy will be printed out and you will be given two minutes to read that letter.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Would you like an opportunity to read the entirety, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean this letter? No. I'm interested in the letter from the Rogatica Brigade because, you see, we only communicated in part; for example, supplies, work assignments, food, et cetera. We never got any professional assignments from the MUP or from the military except to give this kind of logistical support. So I assume that this letter was in that spirit but I need to see the letter of the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: When you say you never got any professional assignments, you did in fact receive reports on what they were doing and requests for assistance, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not what they were doing. Those would be professional assignments, theirs and the police. But in terms of supplies, logistics, and perhaps deploying people for work assignments, work duty, for example, they'd work in a factory or elsewhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So you never discussed, for instance, at Crisis Staff sessions ongoing issues related to territorial defence and protection of the Serbian people?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I would say only to the extent to which it applies to logistics; namely, what is necessary for these formations to exist excluding weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: What about the activities of the army and its incorporation into the army of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, did that come up at Crisis Staff sessions? And if it would assist we can call back up P3913.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is the letter to which this letter refers, is that letter available?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I can say I haven't located it, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You haven't located it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: When we get P3913 back up, we'll be looking at page 3 in the English and also in the B/C/S. I'm looking for the third paragraph in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And it reads: "The agenda that was discussed at the Crisis Staff sessions included basic agenda items from the Crisis Staff domain; i.e., the ongoing issues referring to the domain of territorial defence and protection of the Serbian people and its property, supplying people with all types of essential goods, estimation of political and security situation in the area of the municipality, the activities of the army and its incorporation into the Army of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and other similar issues." So I'd put to you that in fact you were aware of the military formations in the area. You did communicate with them not entirely about logistic issues but also about matters within their military domain, and so your statement to the Rogatica police in 2004 was not correct.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not accept that because I think that all of the statements were responsible ones. We never dealt with concrete issues related to the work of the army or the police, but I have to tell you that we provided full support when the VRS was established to have that component function, and we always supported it only in the domain of logistics.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have no further questions for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I do tender the last two documents that I used which are 65 ter 31354, the letter from the Executive Committee, and 31333, the Rogatica MUP interview of Mr. Sokolovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, the first one, the letter.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Will be Exhibit P6775, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted. The second one, the interview.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Will be Exhibit P6776, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence. Mr. Stojanovic, any further questions for the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A few, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sokolovic, during your examination today, there was discussion about abrogating the agreement on the division of the Rogatica municipality into the Serb and Muslim parts. What led to that decision made by the municipality of Rogatica to abrogate that agreement?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before answering, I wish to recall the following. The municipality of Rogatica was never divided in the urban area, that is to say the centre of Rogatica, so a population of 8.500 and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, Witness, you're here to answer questions, not to --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- tell us what you find relevant and important but rather to answer the questions that are put to you by Mr. Stojanovic at this moment. What caused it to abrogate?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First of all, I apologise, Mr. President, and let me respond once again. I would put it this way: The situation changed in the territory of the municipality of Rogatica. The population became homogenous and the Muslim population, that was the majority population. Until then Rogatica was a town under control and they started moving in two directions, to the south and to the west, and therefore it was believed that control should be exercised over that territory, that life should be organised, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: From a military and security point of view, who was the first to infringe upon the agreement between you and the Muslim people in Rogatica?
