utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Muslims or rather their leadership.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have P6773 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, could you assist me, do we have a text of such an agreement?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, unfortunately no. I tried together with the witness to try to find this agreement, however we didn't manage to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I think we may have a copy and I'm just going to look around our system, but I believe we have a copy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Stojanovic, first of all, you of course could have asked Mr. Traldi to provide it to you; but second, if you say who was the first to infringe upon the agreement, any answer to that question, of course, depends on what was agreed. And if the Chamber has no copy of the agreement, then of course the answer lacks quite a bit of probative value. Meanwhile, proceed, and Mr. Traldi will try to find it, I take it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I hope that this will be helpful to us and how.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Please take a look at this document in front of you. This is a document that you had the opportunity of seeing today when the Prosecutor was cross-examining. In the third paragraph, the last sentence, because the war conflict broke out --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second. Yes, we are now on the second page in the English language as well. Please proceed. No loud speaking, Mr. Mladic. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The last sentence in the third paragraph says because the war conflict broke out, the Serb assembly of the municipality of Rogatica passed a decision to the effect that the entire territory of the municipality of Rogatica would be declared a Serb municipality. At that moment, when did you as the executive organ believe that war conflict broke out in the municipality of Rogatica?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think the war conflict broke out on St. George's day, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And I will end my questioning on this document. What is the date of St. George's day, according to the orthodox Christian calendar?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is the 6th of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now look together at a document that we have seen before, 65 ter 31352. 31352, page 6 of this statement. I'm sorry, page 3 of this statement in English, third paragraph from the top. And in B/C/S, it would be page 4. Page 5, the third paragraph from the top in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Before I ask you a question about this paragraph --

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mehmed Agic was the commander of the Territorial Defence in Rogatica before the war, a reserve officer, and I would say that he was a renowned military expert.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In this statement that was quoted to you a moment ago regarding the malt factory, in this paragraph, and my colleague tells me it was recorded a little differently, I am showing the third paragraph from the bottom, not the top, he says: "In March 1992, a large number of inhabitants of Rogatica, driven by feelings of fear, insecurity, and uncertainty about further developments moved out of the town and found shelter in Central Bosnia, Gorazde, Zepa, and the wider Vragolovo area." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You've read a portion of this document. Mr. Traldi is on his feet. Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. It's very different than the portion of the document I read. I'm not sure how it arises from my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's one issue I'd like you to respond to, Mr. Stojanovic. The second one is you said: "... in this paragraph, and my colleague tells me it was recorded a little differently..." Now, it's unclear to me what recording you are referring to and what is recorded differently, because without such an explanation we would have problems in understanding your reference to this inaccuracy. So first, does it arise from the cross-examination, and could you tell us in what respect?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So, the answer to the first question, I was told that the record shows I was dealing with the third paragraph from the top whereas I meant the third paragraph from the bottom. And now I believe it is correctly recorded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That having now been verified. Next question is: How does this arise from cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I believe you had occasion to see a number of questions asked by Mr. Traldi in his cross-examination that related to the time when the population departed from Rogatica. And this paragraph speaks precisely to that, the time when people departed from Rogatica and the reasons for their departure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may put the question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With your leave, Your Honour, I would like to consult my client for a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, Mr. Sokolovic, my question is: Is it the case and would you tell the Court, to the best of your recollection, at which point in time did the Muslim population leave Rogatica?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll try. They left in two batches to Zepa which became more numerous. This part in April, buses and cars to Sarajevo of their own free will, and eventually, in the end, people were led towards the south, led by the president of the municipality and his associates, and to the west, led by this Mehmed Agic. They crossed over to Praca river, followed the canyon to Ustipraca, and all together they went to Gorazde.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did all that happen before the first fighting, before the first armed conflicts in Rogatica?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The first part was in the spring in normal circumstances, and after the armed conflicts and killings, even the killings of Serbs in the part of Rogatica controlled by Muslims, these two columns followed, one to the south, and one to the west. And that is when Rogatica remained with very few inhabitants in the area of the town and thus the municipality.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, first of all you started your next question before the interpretation had been finished. I'm still trying to fully understand the testimony. The first part was in the spring. Is that your reference to what you said the first batch in April?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Would you please tell the Court, to the best of your recollection, what did this complex called the Sladara consist of? Could you enumerate all its parts?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most of all there were production capacities, a silo of barley, some garages, some workshops, and that was the largest part. And the smaller part was the administration building which held offices, a canteen, some small warehouses, and that office space was used by the municipal organs of Rogatica, and there was also a depot in this part of the building of the Red Cross.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see the clock, Your Honours. I don't think I need more than ten minutes. Perhaps this is a good time for the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Unless you would like to finish in those ten minutes and then take the break slightly later, but if you prefer to take the break now, then it's okay as far as I'm concerned. I have, however, one other question for you. You said that Mr. Agic was exchanged. Do you have any knowledge about these exchanges, because in your statement we find information about people voluntarily leaving. But do you have any knowledge about these exchanges?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I don't. But I have to say I heard about Mr. Agic later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Fine. Then if you have no knowledge, that's an answer to my question. We'll take a break after the witness has left the courtroom. Mr. Traldi, could you give us an indication as to how much time you would need anticipating on what could happen in ten minutes?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I know a lot can happen in ten minutes, Mr. President. Right now, a minute or two, very little. What I'd risen for was to refer Mr. Stojanovic to Exhibit P3026. Now, that's what I'd had in mind when he -- when we were discussing the agreement. My understanding is it's a map that reflects it rather than the text of the agreement itself. But that's what I'd had had in mind and I wanted to refer him to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Which doesn't make it easy for us to find out what exactly the probative value is of saying that one party violated the agreement, infringed upon the agreement first, if it's only a map. We take a break and we resume at 25 minutes past 12.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are waiting for the witness to be escorted into the courtroom. Meanwhile, I raise one matter, Mr. Lukic. It is uncommon that counsel who is not examining the witness intervenes and objects during the examination. I'm not going to make a formal point out of that but it surprised me somewhat. Again, I'm not going to make any formal point. And I'm still waiting for your references to, and let's be very precise on that, on not intervening during the Prosecution's case when a witness had shown a clear misunderstanding of what his role was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Because testimony of witnesses being contradicted by documentary evidence, that happens almost every day and that is, in my view, part, a normal part of cross-examination, but I specifically responded at that point in time to an expression of the witness who clearly demonstrated not to understand what his role was. And I'm looking forward to see whether I used any double standards, and I will seriously look into any reference you'll give me. Even if it's 500, I'll read them all. I take it that I can expect it within a week or something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we call up in e-court, Your Honours, P3193 again. Sorry, 3913. 3913. Sorry, it was my mistake. Could we look at page 6, paragraph 8 in both versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sokolovic, that's the report on which Mr. Traldi asked you a couple of things. I would just like to direct your attention to the last paragraph on this page. And then at some point, we have to move to the next page in both versions. It reads: "The process of complete transformation was accompanied by many difficulties so that the transformation is not complete yet. In the territory of Rogatica municipality, instead of units of the Territorial Defence, it is the Rogatica Brigade of the Army of Republika Srpska of Bosnia-Herzegovina is active and it is part of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can you direct us in the English where you are reading. We saw a paragraph at the beginning but then the interpretation differed from what's on the page.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: If the interpreter may be of assistance, it's the top of the English page. Only the word "order" is different.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Stojanovic. And the interpreters are thanked.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, the last sentence. "The Crisis Staff is not authorised to underline the activities and actions of the Territorial Defence units, later the army of Rogatica Brigade, its successes and failures and other military issues in its report." In this period when you were active as the Executive Board and the Crisis Staff from April to June of 1992, why did you emphasise that it is not within your competence to stress it in your reports?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We cared to say that because people were not sufficiently aware of various jurisdictions and there were frequent misunderstandings as to who is supposed to do what. And that's why we always emphasised that everybody had their own missions and assignments to take care of, whereas other people were in charge of other things. People had various versions, you could hear all sorts of talk but that didn't matter. What mattered were the real competencies, purviews, and jurisdictions.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I would like to conclude one topic relating to P6774. This is a document you've seen before. It was shown to you by the Prosecution earlier today. The Prosecutor asked you if you had seen this document before, and I want to ask you about something that is mentioned in the document. Did you know, and if so how did you know, that there were problems between Muslims who had declared themselves willing to remain in Rogatica and those Muslims who had decided to leave?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have any documents to rely on, but it was my feeling that there were serious differences between one number of people, mainly old timers, natives of Rogatica, and some others who did not set it as their objective to stay in Rogatica.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Apparently you're asking about frictions between the various groups of Muslims. I do not see how this arises from cross-examination because I don't think that it has been touched upon in any way by Mr. Traldi. But you have put the question to the witness, the witness has answered it. Any further questions or was it --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honours, thank you. I am concluding my redirect examination. Thank you for your understanding.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stojanovic. Judge Moloto has one or more questions for you. Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Sokolovic, I really want to get some clarity. I know you've given a large amount of evidence according -- relating to your tenure as president of the Executive Committee or the assembly of the municipality. If you look at paragraph 2 of your statement, please, it says: "In the early 1990s, I was a deputy in the Rogatica municipal assembly. I also served as the president of the Rogatica municipal assembly in two, one-year terms, specifically 1983 and 1985. At the end of 1991 and the beginning of 1992, I served as a deputy in the Rogatica municipal assembly. I performed this duty from 1978 to 2008." Do you remember that paragraph?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do, and it's the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Now, what I would like to understand is -- because later in your evidence, you then said you served as a president from 1983 to 1985. You said this at yesterday's temporary transcript page 77, lines 9 to 10. Now, when you say 1983 to 1985, it's different from saying two one-year terms in 1983 and 1985. If you could clear us on that point first.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll explain that very easily. I was talking about two one-year terms, one began in spring 1983, and the other began in the spring of 1984 and lasted until 1985. So these were the two one-year terms.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Now, again on this paragraph as I said you said, in the early 1990s, I was deputy of the Rogatica municipal assembly, and you say at the end of 1991 and the beginning of 1992 you served as the deputy in the Rogatica municipal ... and because I think for purposes of this case it is the period 1992 that is relevant, I just want to be sure in that period when were you deputy and when were you president in the period 1991 and 1992?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You see I was a deputy in 1991 and 1992, continuously. I was an MP in the municipal parliament. As for the function of vice-president, I don't know if it was recorded that I was also vice-president. I was a regular deputy even before but from 1990, in 1991, and 1992, I was also vice-president. I was vice-president of the assembly in earlier terms of office and again after the war.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do you make a distinction between deputy and vice? Are those two different positions?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly vice-president is an official, whereas a deputy to the parliament is just a member of parliament.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: When you say "deputy" just you mean being a member of the assembly?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I must say I'm still puzzled by the whole of it. Could we have your statement on the screen so that you can follow in B/C/S the text of your statement. But I don't know the number by heart. The statement has received number.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: D652, I think, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D652. Could we focus on paragraph 2. I go with you through every sentence of this paragraph. You started saying: "In the early 1990s, I was a deputy in the Rogatica Municipal Assembly." The next line reads: "I also served as the president of the Rogatica municipal assembly in two one-year terms, specifically in 1983 and 1985." You explained what that meant, that is, that you served as president from spring 1983 and then until 1984 and then from 1984 to 1985. I have some difficulties in understanding that where you say in the early 1990s you were a deputy, that you say you were a president in 1983 and 1984 which are not, in my view, the 1990s. Are you talking about the same Rogatica Municipal Assembly here? When you are talking about the early 1990s, which Rogatica Municipal Assembly are you talking about? Is that the multi-ethnic elected municipal assembly or is it a different one?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely that one, the one that was elected at the first multi-parties elections in 1990.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When you say you were a president of the Rogatica Municipal Assembly in two one-year terms, 1983, 1985, was that the same assembly?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So therefore, you served already on that assembly not only in the early 1990s but even before that in the 1980s.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From 1978 all the way up to 2008.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So this is totally confusing language. I don't know who took this statement but -- so I have to understand that from the late 1970s, you were a deputy in the Rogatica Municipal Assembly where you served as a president in two one-year terms in 1983 and 1984 ending in 1985. Now, the next line reads: "At the end of 1991 and the beginning of 1992, I served as a deputy in the Rogatica Municipal Assembly." Which assembly are you referring to there? To the same assembly or to the Serb assembly?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, the same one. The same assembly. You see, the war came, relations were disrupted, but the term of office went on from 1991 and then 1992, and all the way up until the end of the war there weren't any elections. The elections were held only in 1996.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand your answer. However, the end of 1991 happens to be exactly the time when the Serb Municipal Assembly was established at the instructions of the SDS Main Board, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but for a while this regular assembly operated along parallel lines as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And the beginning of 1992 was exactly that period in time where, as you said, it functioned parallel with the multi-ethnic elected assembly.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So therefore, everyone who is familiar with the evidence in this case would easily understand a reference to the end of 1991 and the beginning of 1992 as a reference rather to the Serb assembly rather than the multi-ethnic elected assembly.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If necessary, I am prepared to clarify this further, but the essence is the following: the Serb municipal assembly started working a bit more seriously only in the spring but along parallel lines. All the time the elected assembly functioned and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's the reason. Since you do not say anything explicitly about the Serb municipal assembly, it gives the impression that this is a kind of a puzzle or a hidden reference to an assembly functioning at the same time without saying this clearly. Otherwise, I'm totally missing any understanding for how this paragraph was drafted in the statement. I don't know who took this statement. At least I leave that alone. But it's clear to me now where everything suggests that you are not very transparent on the Serb municipal assembly, to say the least, that paragraph 2 may look as if it hints at the existence and your participation in such a Serb assembly in Rogatica. Do you have any comment on what I just said?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, briefly. I'm sorry if there's anything that's unclear there, but again I wish to recall the following: In this paragraph, I only speak about the regular assembly, that is to say, the one elected at the multi-national elections. It was elected in 1990 and it went on until 1996. That's when the elections were held. In the meantime, the Serb municipality of Rogatica was constituted and automatically, I became a member of that assembly as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you have explained that. I have understood that. At the same time for the taking of a statement, and I'm now addressing the Defence, this confusion is -- could be expected if the statement is phrased in the way it did. I leave it to that. Any further questions, Mr. Traldi?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Just about three, Your Honour, although Judge Moloto, did you have a question first?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just one. Just to be clear, this last sentence where you say: "I performed this duty from 1978 to 2008." Are we to understand that for all that period, 1978 to 2008, you were a member of the Rogatica Municipal Assembly?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Which means at the beginning of the paragraph when you say in the early 1990s I was a member of the Rogatica municipality, that's half the truth because the truth is that you were a member from 1978 to 2008. So that first sentence is redundant and unnecessary. Do I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it may be that way as well, but believe me this is the truth, that I was a member of the municipal assembly for 30 years without any interruptions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. That makes it quite clearer, much clearer. Because now the first sentence seems to suggest that that was the only time in addition to the 1992 one. Okay. Thank you so much. Yes, Mr. Traldi. Further cross-examination by Mr. Traldi:

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, in response to the Judge's questions you said you were the vice-president of the assembly, was that the elected assembly or the Serb assembly?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The regularly-elected assembly but serving several terms, you see. It's always this lawful municipal assembly from 1978 until 2008.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Just to make sure I understood your answer to the Judges' questions properly, I understood you to be saying that at some point between 1991 and 1995 you'd also held the position of vice-president of one of the assemblies; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Moving to a different topic. Sir, Mr. Stojanovic asked you about the timing of people leaving Rogatica. You said some of those who left Rogatica in 1992 went to Zepa; right? And before that? After Zepa fell in 1995, there were almost no Muslims left in Rogatica municipality at all; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but they left Zepa along a different route. You know how they left.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber has no further questions either -- yes, one question. Further questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just to be clear. Is it your evidence that at no stage in your life have you ever been a member of the Serb assembly of the Rogatica municipality? In other words, the one that's not elected?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We have to explain that. I was a member of the regular assembly all the time, and according to the decision of the Serb municipality of Rogatica, all members of the assembly who were ethnic Serbs from the regular assembly became members of the Serb municipal assembly of Rogatica. That is the autumn of 1991.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There being no further questions, Mr. Sokolovic, I'd like to thank you for coming a long way to The Hague and for having answered all the questions that were put to you by the parties and by the Bench and I wish you a safe return home again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, and I would like to thank you for having treated me so fairly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'll ask to be excused as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You are excused.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The -- may I take it that the next witness the Defence intends to call is -- let me just have a look, is Mr. Sarenac.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, that's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The usher has left the courtroom as well. I take the time to previously address P6680 and immediately after we've done that we can start the examination of the next witness. During the testimony of Milutin Vujicic on the 17th of July of this year, P6680, the Foca gazette No. 1, was marked for identification after the Prosecution indicated that the parties would discuss a possible agreement on only whether certain portions of P6680 should be tendered. On the 25th of August, the Prosecution informed the Chamber through an informal communication that the parties had agreed to tender the entire document. On the 26th of August, the Chamber, noting that the document is 74 pages long, informed the parties that it was not inclined to admit it in its entirety and gave the parties one week to file submissions explaining why they deem it necessary to admit the document in it's entirety rather than the portions that were discussed with the witness. This can be found at transcript pages 24766 to 24767. Mr. Usher you can already escort the witness into the courtroom while I'm -- continue reading. On the 1st of September, the Prosecution filed its written submissions. The Prosecution submits that the document should be admitted in it's entirety because it is important to understand the events and the political structure in Foca municipality during the conflict.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Alternatively, the Prosecution submits that the Chamber should admit those pages of the document that were discussed with the witness in court. The Defence did not make any submissions. Mr. Sarenac, could I invite you to be seated for a little while. I will continue to read and once I finished, I will address you as a witness. The Chamber recalls that each party is responsible for presenting its case in a clear and comprehensible manner and therefore underlines the importance of the parties' assistance in placing documentary evidence, especially large exhibits, in the context of the indictment. This is best done when the exhibit is used with the witness in court. Lacking this contextualisation, the Chamber may not fully appreciate the reason a party relies on a document. With regard to P6680, the Chamber notes that the witness, when confronted with the decision to establish the assembly of the Serbian people in Foca municipality, was able to provide information on the meaning of certain parts of it. When confronted with the Statute of the Serbian municipality of Foca, the witness confirmed that he knew that such a Statute had been adopted. Therefore, the Chamber finds that these two portions were sufficiently contextualised by the witness. The Trial Chamber is not convinced, however, that the remaining portions of P6680 without any contextualisation assist the Chamber. In its submission of the 1st of September, the Prosecution merely submitted that Foca is an important municipality and that P6680 provides important background to understand the events in Foca. The Chamber considers that such a lax standard would be conducive to a flooding of the Chamber with documentary evidence, which it has consistently tried to avoid. Therefore, the Chamber admits pages 1 to 4 and 12 to 31 of the English translation -- 32, I misread, 12 to 32 of the English translation of P6680, as well as the corresponding pages in the original into evidence, and denies admission of the remaining pages without prejudice. The Prosecution is instructed to upload a new version of P6680 reflecting the Chamber's decision and the Registry is already hereby instructed to make the necessary replacement thereafter. This concludes the Chamber's decision on the admission of P6680. Mr. Sarenac, apologies for being so impolite as not addressing you when you entered the courtroom. Before you give evidence, you are invited to make a solemn declaration. The text of which is now handed out to you. May I invite you to do so.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please be seated. Mr. Sarenac, you will first be examined by Mr. Lukic -- I take it, Mr. Lukic? Mr. Lukic is counsel for Mr. Mladic and you will find him to your left. Mr. Lukic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Mr. Sarenac.

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR SARENAC
utterances.text: Good day.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would just ask for the help from the usher. I have to distribute something first so we can continue in a speedy manner. I would just hand the clean copy of Mr. Sarenac statement to him, just for the Prosecution first to check, and I have some documents to be given to the Judges, Prosecution, and the witness. I will draw Your Honours' attention when we have to look at a document I just distributed separate from the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Sarenac --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And, yes, can we have on our screens, 1D01742, that's the statement of this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Sarenac, you have before you the paper version and on the screen, you see the first page of the document?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR SARENAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It's Milorad Sokolovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I can see that. Yeah. That's the number I have. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So let us restart. Mr. Sarenac, have you ever given a statement to the members of General Mladic's Defence team?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR SARENAC
utterances.text: Yes, I gave a statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is that the statement that you have before you now?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR SARENAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And what you see on the screen, is that the first page of that statement?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR SARENAC
utterances.text: Yes, that's the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you sign this statement?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR SARENAC
utterances.text: Yes, this is my signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let's take a look at the last page now. Do you see a signature there?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR SARENAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you recognise it?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR SARENAC
utterances.text: Yes, that is my signature and the date is the 27th of July, 2014.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Does this statement contain what you said to the members of the Defence team of General Mladic?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR SARENAC
utterances.text: Yes, that's the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The information contained in this statement, is it correct?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR SARENAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If I were to put the same questions to you today, would you basically answer them the same way?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR SARENAC
utterances.text: I would certainly answer them the same way.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Usually I miss some of the questions on the introduction, but we do not Judge Fluegge today with us so I took care that everything is covered. So I think that I covered everything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: He'll be glad that you took over part of his responsibilities.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So I would tender this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The last one was -- okay. No, you covered it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you want to take over? I would like to tender this statement into evidence, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar -- but perhaps first, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Provided it's the same one that was filed, the Prosecution has no objections. Although if there's any problem, I'd just -- I'm noticing some font differences with the one here so -- I'll just check that. But provided it's the same, no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, it is the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It is the same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then Mr. Weber will have a hard job to find any differences. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, 65 ter number 1D1742 will be D653.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D653 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would read a statement summary and then have just couple of questions for this witness, with your leave. Thank you. Desimir Sarenac was chief of security in the 1st Sarajevo Brigade. He will testify about the positions held by his unit, his operational position, and its strength. He will also testify about positions held by opposing units of the 1st Corps of the Army of B and H and its strength. He will testify that the SRK was mainly engaged in defensive actions. Also, he will testify that the SRK had no intention to cause casualties, civilian casualties during combat or terrorise the civilians under the control of Muslim authorities. Furthermore, he will testify that he had some information that civilian facilities were being misused for military purposes by the 1st Corps of the ABiH. Desimir Sarenac will testify about the security situation in and around the area of responsibility of the 1st Sarajevo Brigade. He will testify about the discipline in his brigade. Also, he will testify about paramilitaries in the zone of responsibility of the 1st Sarajevo Brigade. He will testify on overall situation in Sarajevo, before and after conflict emerged.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No speaking at such volume that it disturbs the order in the courtroom. Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. He will testify as to situation in Sarajevo during withdrawal of JNA, leaving of its members, and grave situation in Sarajevo. He will explain zone of responsibility of his units, its composition, organisation, and functioning in relevant period. Witness will testify as to the illegal arming of Croats and Muslims and organising of paramilitary units in Sarajevo, as from the beginning of the conflict. He will testify that his unit performed no offensive activity, and that it was focused to preserve its lines during the period of conflict. He will testify as to positions of enemy units in, and around Sarajevo, and information obtained through operative work. He will testify as to position of superior command of SRK towards use of artillery in the city, and on the other side on Army of B and H strategy of opening fire from civilian zones, schools, and hospitals, towards position of SRK units, or even attacking civilian zones on their own territory for blaming the Serb side. He will explain ABiH positioning in and around the city during the period of conflict. He will also testify as to using snipers from Army of B and H side and its consequences towards civilians. Witness will explain that civilians could not leave Sarajevo during conflict on their own will and without security threats. That would be his statement summary, and I will just have several questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please put them to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Sarenac, now I'm going to ask you something. The Prosecution objected to two exhibits that we tendered as associated exhibits.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now I'd like to call up 1D4398 in e-court. [In English] If we can have only B/C/S version because it's the map, and we have English translation in front of us in paper distributed for everybody. If we can enlarge the middle part of this map, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Sarenac, there is a key to this map and you have it before you. What did you show on this map?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR SARENAC
utterances.text: I marked the positions of Muslim armed formations as juxtaposed to my brigade, the deployment of firing assets, and the places where ammunition and weapons were manufactured. I also marked the command posts of their units for a certain period considering that the positions of units changed over time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What period do your markings relate to?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR SARENAC
utterances.text: Essentially it's all the same. What varies is the numerical strength of units, but the strength of the enemy side only increased with time. According to the documents that I had at my disposal when I made this map, and that is 18 months ago, and based on my memory, I made an oversight in relation to Dobrinja. My markings venture inside the area held by the enemy side. Our positions were closer to Lukavica, that's something that I can correct now.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This key to the map, does it correspond to the signs you made on the map?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR SARENAC
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Are your markings precise or off?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR SARENAC
utterances.text: Of course they are not precise. This is just a graphic display and on a city map, on a street plan, you cannot identify all the streets and all the buildings. I only tried to show where we were and where they were without being able to be precise. But as far as the number of units and the strength is concerned, I did not include the number of units or the number of ammunition producing facilities. It's not even possible to show this on this map and you cannot show it in a proper size.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You made this map during the Karadzic trial; correct?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR SARENAC
utterances.text: It was on the 5th of March, 2013, based on the documents that I had at my disposal.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you draw all the positions indicated in the documents you had, or can we find more in the documents than on the map?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR SARENAC
utterances.text: As for the forward line, the answer is yes, that's how the forward line really lay with the exception of Dobrinja where I made a mistake. For the rest, I did not have the means to show it all precisely. But basically, that's a fair representation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We would tender this map with attached legend into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before we do that, Mr. Lukic, if you look at page 2 of the legend, last two items are not translated into English. Can we be told what they are?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. I'm sorry because -- I was translating this from English so that's why I didn't see that there are only some B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You can translate it back to English then.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sarenac, turn to page 2 and you will see at the bottom there are two notes, OBL and VP in B/C/S. Can you read them for us?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR SARENAC
utterances.text: OBL unit for the protection of installations and units.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And the second one?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR SARENAC
utterances.text: Military police.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I believe that right now we're at the point where Mr. Lukic is tendering the map. Mr. Lukic addressed our concerns so the Prosecution does not have an objection to it. However, we've looked at many maps with many symbols and now we have one with symbols again in them. I appreciate the fact that there's a legend for what this witness understands these symbols to be. However, I believe at this point it would be of great assistance to the Chamber to have 65 ter 30651, which is the JNA instructions on maps in the armed forces, before it so -- as a reference material. It contains the various symbols that are used by the armed forces, and I just throw that out to the Chamber right now, not necessarily looking for a decision, but I believe that this could be of aid to the Chamber if the Defence could also assist in reviewing that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And of course we do not know whether it corresponds fully with the legend the witness has given, but if the parties would sit together and see whether there's any dispute about that and then to tender it by one party or by another party in the context of this testimony. Before we decide on admission, I would have one question, Mr. Sarenac. I see more or less the front lines and you corrected them as far as Dobrinja is concerned. That's all fine. But I see that there is a kind of a line going into north-westerly direction, or if you start at the other side, the south-easterly direction, between Novi Grad and Alipasino Polje. You see that? Where it just moves away from what seems to be the separation lines. Could you explain to us how this almost like a pin, line a needle into the area of -- ending in Alipasino Polje, what that stands for exactly? It's a double line, by the way, and it's an interrupted line, a double interrupted line. I should be more precise.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Judge, I'm not sure it's before the witness on the screen.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's the boundary between the 5th Motorised Brigade and the --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness repeat the second unit?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Could the witness repeat the second unit, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's the demarcation between you said the 5th Motorised Brigade and what was the other unit you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And the 101st Motorised Brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So we also have to understand, for example, that where we find the similar line ending up in Otoka, that that also indicates the separation between units, and may I then take it Army ABiH units?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that is it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Then finally, you explained to us what OBL stands for and what VP stands for. Could you point at anywhere where there is a military police station, so where we find a VP? I may have even found one. I see one. I withdraw that question. I see that there are some of them. No further objections. Then, Mr. Registrar, the map --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. 65 ter 1D4398 will be Exhibit D654.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D654 is admitted into evidence. The legend to the map, Mr. Lukic, has it been uploaded into e-court?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Under what number? Because it seems -- or is it attached to the map?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's attached to the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's attached to the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Only is it -- it serves as an English version of the map. That was how it was done in Karadzic case as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Only now we have this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- B/C/S translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No problems. So the legend -- so I have admitted the legend already into evidence without knowing it. Yes. Yes, now, if you say it is attached, and you said to the English version -- it's the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's the English version, yeah, of the B/C/S map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'd just check. Yes, I understand. So as a matter of fact, we have here a document on which the English version is just the legend and the original B/C/S version is just the map as marked by the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it's clear to me. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's a break time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It indeed is break time. We'll take a break and we'll resume at ten minutes to 2.00 but not until after the witness has left the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We're waiting for the witness to be escorted into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Judge, maybe I could just make use of the time with some housekeeping matters related to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, if you look behind --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- Mr. Weber --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- you can see that you should have started earlier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. We don't need this map in e-court, but I would like to have 1D03018.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, with respect to this exhibit, but it also, I believe, applies to 21 exhibits related to the witness, and this is just a technical matter first, the Prosecution's records indicate that it's not a part of the Defence 65 ter exhibit list, so if just for formality's sake if we could have a request to add this exhibit to the exhibit list. Then I do have an objection to the use of the document after that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Well, then we would formally ask for these exhibits to be added.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Let's decide on them together. Let's not lose too much time on formalities. But before we do so, Mr. Lukic, you said we don't need this map in e-court, but I take it that if you don't want to have it in e-court, how would you like to have it -- on our screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I thought I -- no, no. I needed a different document on our screen. That's why I said we don't need this one anymore.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh, you mean the map we had looked at before.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that wasn't clear to me. Yes. Then the document announced now --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I asked for 1D03018.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, which is requested to be added to your 65 ter list and that's -- then we would like to hear from Mr. Weber what the objections are.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution would object to the use of this document with this specific witness. It's described to us as a list of patients in the Kasindol hospital. Our objection relates to the fact that as far as we're aware this individual has no medical knowledge or expertise and we have some concern about the Chamber receiving medically related evidence not coming through a qualified individual or expert in demographics or otherwise, so I'd also note that the Karadzic Defence elected not to use this document with this witness in the past proceedings. So we have concern about our ability to even be able to cross-examine a witness who probably does not have the necessary basis of knowledge or expertise to be able to sufficiently comment on a lot of the information, and we believe it should not be used properly with this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think it's just fair to let us ask several questions and then decide whether this witness knows anything about the contents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The objection, what the objection was about, the objection was about the use. But, Mr. Weber, I see your point that you say it -- the list apparently is based on who are the most serious ones. Now, that's one issue. But of course there were other elements in it as well; that is, were these people, apart from whether they are the most serious ones, were they treated in Kasindol hospital, and you don't need medical expert knowledge for that. If you know those persons, if you see them going into the hospital and you accompany them. I do not know -- I've got no idea what kind of knowledge this witness has, but your objection is not solid for all circumstances so therefore I will allow Mr. Lukic to ask questions, but as soon as of course it comes down to expert testimony, then it's a different matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, and right now we have no notice of the fact that this witness has any involvement with the Kasindol hospital so that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Neither do we. So that is for Mr. Lukic to explore. Mr. Lukic, you use the document. We'll later decide on whether or not --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I promise that I will not try to elicit any expert opinions from this witness on this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us look at the document. On page 1 we read "Seriously injured civilians, 1992, 1995 undergoing treatment at Kasindol hospital." Let me ask you, was it usual, was it customary that civilians who lived in the zone of replenishment of your unit be sent for treatment at the Kasindol hospital?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR SARENAC
utterances.text: Of course. It was normal. The hospital treated both uniformed personnel and civilians.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The witness has answered the question by just asking a future question, so if Counsel could please be mindful of leading the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, and then for me, just to see. One second please. Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Apart from civilians, was anyone else from the zone of your replenishment treated at this hospital?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR SARENAC
utterances.text: As for me personally, on the 13th of June, 1993, I was wounded in combat at Mojmilo and the soldier next to me was killed. Since my injury was not so serious, it was in the left upper arm, I didn't go the same day. I went to the Kasindol hospital a day or two later where Dr. Srdjan Mijatovic took out the fragmented bullet casing out of my arm, and on that occasion I saw other wounded people there. As for sniping, that zone was very exposed and one of the incidents I remember most vividly is the death of one old man who was hit on the doorstep of his house.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me stop you there. Mr. Lukic asked you apart from civilians was anyone else from the zone of your replenishment treated at this hospital. Now, Mr. Lukic, the witness goes in all kind of directions. Either you guide him in that direction or stop him by giving rather -- statements without any context as to when, where, who, et cetera. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And in fact, Mr. Lukic, by the time you asked that question, the witness had already told us before that of course it was normal. The hospital treated both uniformed personnel and civilians. So the question was clearly redundant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And then else -- apparently you wanted to ask him anyone else than you yourself. That was not part of the question. It took me two or three lines to understand what the question was about. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you know if the Kasindol hospital treated wounded people regardless of ethnicity and do you have any firsthand knowledge?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR SARENAC
utterances.text: I know that. This Dr. Srdjan Mijatovic who I already mentioned, he had served as a doctor in our outpatient clinic before, before transferring to the hospital. And at the time when I went to the hospital for that shrapnel to be extracted, he told me that several injured civilians had been brought in during the past days, especially from Grbavica, Serb civilians and Muslims.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, is there any -- is it part of the Prosecution's case that in this hospital, civilians were not treated or that there was any distinction made on the basis of ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: We disagree with the context that the witness is describing it in but not that there were civilians that were treated in the hospital along with soldiers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And of all ethnicities?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Well, the context of non-Serbs -- I will cross-examine on this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. If we can have page 2 of this document. In English it's not translated so we'll have to use -- but those are only names, but we'll read the whole line.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You mentioned a man by the name of Trapara who was killed by a sniper shot. Did you know any of his relatives? Was that person wounded, did you visit him in hospital, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR SARENAC
utterances.text: I knew Bosko Trapara personally. I knew his son and daughter and his daughter also had a restaurant. I also knew two relatives of his who had the same last name, Trapara. They were elderly women. It was Duda or something like that, Dubravka, and the other one is Bosijlka [phoen] and they were seriously injured by a sniper. I used to know quite a few such cases but at this moment I cannot remember all the names.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Please look at 28. Could you read out the entire line for us.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We cannot hear the witness if he's not speaking directly into the microphone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, Witness, could you please, if you're bowing towards your screen, keep your mind that you should speak into the microphone because the interpreters would not hear you. Could you restart your answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Trapara Dusanka Dubravka, female, born in 1921, Kasindol, Ilidza, wounded on the 4th of November, 1992 by a shell.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you see Mrs. Trapara anywhere after she was wounded?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR SARENAC
utterances.text: Since I communicated with Bosko's son Drago, and that was close to my barracks and close to the place where I was staying, so we used to see each other there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you ever visit Mrs. Trapara in hospital?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR SARENAC
utterances.text: Well, no, there wasn't really an opportunity for that kind of thing. But as for Drago, we commented upon that, her health, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. When you were wounded, when you went to have that shrapnel taken out, did you only talk to the doctor or did you talk to any one of the patients there?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR SARENAC
utterances.text: I mostly talked to the doctor only. When I saw that people were coming to have their wounds treated and bandaged, I mean, that was the context. And then there were these comments too by Dr. Mijatovic that there are many persons who were hit by shrapnel, shells, et cetera, and that they have a lot of work there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We would like to tender this document because we believe that the witness has sufficient knowledge about that in terms of who was being treated in this hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: We would object to the foundation laid by the witness. Actually his knowledge, I believe, is insufficient for it, and even in part possibly incorrect with respect to the few people that the witness has indicated that he did know of. He said according to his information on page 80, lines 20 and 21, that they were seriously injured by a sniper, and then a few lines later we see that one of these individuals, according to this document, was -- the document indicates was injured by a shell. So this is quite different. I believe that without ability to properly cross-examine the witness, a witness with actually direct knowledge was who was treated at the hospital, it should not be allowed with this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber denies the objection. At least the document gives in some respects an opportunity to verify the accuracy or the inaccuracy, the credibility, reliability of the witness and in that respect, the document will be admitted. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D655.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D655 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Judge, just on that, going back to our original concern. We do have concern about relying on the other information that the witness did not know or may not have personal knowledge of that is part of the list without further evidence or proper testimony on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The probative value of the document and the information which allows us to further consider the reliability and the credibility doesn't mean that the Chamber will blindly accept whatever is there on the document on which the witness has not given any evidence, so we'll use it in accordance with the way in which it was introduced.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And -- thank you. And if just before tomorrow, if the Defence could actually inform the Prosecution where does this document come from, it would be appreciated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That was not part of your objection so we have not considered that when we decided to admit. Yes, we still have to ask for a number and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but before I -- before I admitted the document into evidence, I should have decided on the addition to the 65 ter list, but that's of course implicitly granted as well. I would have one question for the witness. Witness, this Kasindol hospital, was that the hospital where many victims of sniper incident or shelling were treated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, it's the only medical institution that was capable of handling that in addition to the military hospital. It was only Kasindol. Today it is a clinic. And absolutely, people were treated there and that is where they were treated primarily.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. When you refer to the military hospital, which one did you refer to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The military hospital that was in Pale where military personnel who were seriously wounded were being treated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But most of the civilian and sometimes military patients who had been the victims of shelling and sniping were treated in Kasindol. Is that correctly understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, especially when -- when there were many wounded persons, so military personnel were treated there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And that would cover the area which is more or less defined by the places where these people were injured, where we see a lot of places familiar to us, Trnovo, Ilidza, all these areas, people would be brought to the Kasindol hospital?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In principle, yes, the Kasindol hospital. And it depended on the situation at the moment in terms of combat, whether they could get to Ilidza and whether they could be driven directly to Pale and so on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And would that be true for victims from Grbavica as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, Grbavica did not have any other medical institution except for Kasindol, so that was the only one and the closest one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge, I'm asking you, if you don't have, of course we'll fully accept that, about the capacity of the Kasindol hospital compared to the military hospital in Pale? Was it three times as big or was it -- or did it receive ten times as much or just half of the number of the patients that would be received by the military hospital? Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Absolutely. The Kasindol hospital is bigger than the military hospital in Pale but how many times bigger, I don't know. It existed before the war as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for those answers. Mr. Lukic. I'm looking at the clock.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just before we move on the clock, for my own edification, Mr. Lukic, for what purpose is this document being tendered? I'm trying to follow.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That this witness is testifying about the civilian victims in the area of replenishment of his unit. So among other things, this is something that show us that the civilians were really injured by military actions conducted by the opposing side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If I could ask one additional question. The document exclusively deals with civilian patients.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This document only with civilian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. [Overlapping speakers] Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: -- kind of the last two questions kind of highlight my concern. Without someone to cross-examine from the hospital, the last two questions posed by Your Honours become quite difficult and it made apparent in counsel's response the way in which the Defence wants to rely on this document which we would object to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but you're revisiting a ruling which was made, Mr. Weber, and we will wait for your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: My concern, Mr. Lukic, is that now the -- if you're saying all these people were civilians, the witness has not gone through the whole list to tell us that these were all civilians. But should we just take his word for that? He doesn't tell us he knows each and every one of these people and he knows that they were civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You are right, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It remains totally unclear, Mr. Lukic, but you're certainly aware of that, that if I say I have a list of 100 people that are civilians, what -- I mean it's not new to you the discussion about what makes someone to a civilian and why could you make mistakes in that respect. But I take it that you're fully aware of that and that's why I said in response to Mr. Weber's objection that of course we'll use it in a way -- and the witness apparently recognises, knows some of these people. Okay, then this document certainly confirms that those persons were treated in that hospital. That's of course of limited probative value, but we'll certainly keep that in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We have to have some trust in the documents, otherwise we have to say we do not trust the documents whatever they say. If --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, that is an extreme position taken, to have matters which are usually contested, that is, who is a civilian who is not, is it because he has a rifle, is it because he is dressed in a certain way, is it because he receives a military pension that's a well known area the dispute, and that of course is different, for example, for the date of birth being noted in a hospital for a patient where there is usually less concern of mistakes. But we'll deal with that. We do understand Mr. Weber's concerns, and we have pointed out to you also that the probative value of such a document has -- certainly has its clear limitations. And if you say we have to trust documents, then I might bring that to your attention now and then as well, although I would not easily do that if there are good reasons to say that the reliability of the document is not always for the full hundred per cent.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Of course. Even us object sometimes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Even you now and then challenge the --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's not unknown to the Chamber. We adjourn for the day. We will resume tomorrow, Wednesday, the 24th of September, 2014, in this same courtroom, I, at 9.30 in the morning. But we'll adjourn only until after the witness has left the courtroom. You may follow the usher but I would like to instruct you that you should not speak with anyone or communicate in whatever way with whomever about your testimony, whether testimony you gave today or still to be given tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mladic, again, no loud speaking. You can consult with counsel after we have adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We resume tomorrow, the 24th, at 9.30.
